title: BogieCopter
description: Tiltable axles and passive wheels combine flight with surface locomotion for inspection.
introduction: BogieCopter explores how an aerial robot can use the surfaces around it. Passive wheels and tiltable axles let the platform combine flight with ground and inclined-surface motion, matching its locomotion to the inspection task.

problem.heading: Use the surface when it can support the robot.
paragraphs: Aerial access is valuable for inspection, but remaining airborne requires the propulsion system to support the vehicle’s weight. A surface can provide support during parts of the mission where free flight is unnecessary.
Changing between flight and supported locomotion requires a mechanical configuration and control strategy that work across different contact conditions, including inclined surfaces.

approach.heading: Adapt the axles to the operating mode.
paragraphs: BogieCopter combines passive wheels with tiltable axles. The configuration supports aerial and surface locomotion, allowing the same robot to fly and to move while in contact with its environment.

The platform study brings together vehicle design and experimental evaluation of different operating modes. Flight, incline traversal and climbing demonstrations show complementary capabilities of the physical prototype.

evidence.label: Surface locomotion
evidence.text: The supplied hardware recordings show inclined-surface movement and climbing with the physical BogieCopter prototype.

evidence.label: Flight capability
evidence.text: A separate indoor flight recording demonstrates that the aerial–ground design retains free-flight capability.

evidence.label: Energy comparison conditions
evidence.text: The paper’s power comparisons depend on operating mode, speed and payload. The demonstrations are not presented as a fixed multiplier for every inspection mission.
